name: Kedar
title: Ishmael's son and ancestor of the Kedarenes
summary: Kedar was the second son of Ishmael and grandson of Abraham. He became the ancestor of a powerful Arab nomadic tribe known as the Kedarenes, who lived in the Syrian-Arabian desert. The Kedarenes were known as skilled archers, merchants, and shepherds, and they are mentioned repeatedly in the prophetic books of the Old Testament.

keyEvents.title: The Birth and Lineage of Kedar
keyEvents.description: Kedar is mentioned as the second son of Ishmael in the genealogy in Genesis. He is part of the fulfillment of God's promise that Ishmael would become the father of twelve princes.

keyEvents.title: Kedar in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Kedar's place in Ishmael's lineage is confirmed in 1 Chronicles, which repeats the genealogy from Genesis.

keyEvents.title: The Tents of Kedar as a Symbol
keyEvents.description: In the Song of Solomon, the tents of Kedar are used as a poetic comparison for dark beauty. The tents of Kedar, made of dark goat hair fabric, were known throughout the ancient world.

keyEvents.title: The Prophecy of Kedar's Fall
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah prophesies that the glory of Kedar will come to an end and that the mighty archers among Kedar's sons will become few. This happened in connection with Assyrian and Babylonian campaigns.

keyEvents.title: Kedar in Jeremiah's Prophecies
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah mentions Kedar in connection with Nebuchadnezzar's campaign against the Arab tribes. The Kedarenes are described as a nomadic people in the desert who were struck by Babylon's power.

keyEvents.title: Kedar in the Book of Psalms
keyEvents.description: The psalmist expresses sorrow at dwelling among the tents of Kedar, used as a picture of living among hostile and warlike peoples far from God's sanctuary.
